chunks: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to me. He said: Bakr b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Tamim b. Bahlul narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Salih b. Abi Salama al-Nasibini narrated to us. He said: Abu Awana narrated to us, from Abi Bishr, from Sa'id b. Jubayr, from A'isha. She said:

I was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, when Ali b. Abi Talib came forward. So he [the Prophet] said: This is the Master of the Arabs. I said: O Messenger of Allah, are you not the Master of the Arabs? He said: I am the Master of the Children of Adam, and Ali is the Master of the Arabs. I said: And what is a Master? He said: One whose obedience was made obligatory, just as obedience to me was made obligatory.

key_terms.افْتُرِضَتْ طَاعَتُهُ: His obedience was made obligatory — indicating divinely-imposed obligation, not mere voluntary respect
key_terms.سَيِّد: Master/leader — one who holds authority; the Prophet defines it as one whose obedience is divinely mandated
key_terms.وَلَد آدَمَ: Children of Adam — all of humanity

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ali being the Master of the Arabs?
ai.summary: In this hadith narrated by A'isha, the Prophet Muhammad (s) bestows upon Ali b. Abi Talib the title 'Master of the Arabs' (sayyid al-Arab). When A'isha asks whether the Prophet himself is not the master of the Arabs, he distinguishes his own status as 'Master of the Children of Adam' from Ali's specific mastership over the Arabs. The Prophet then defines 'master' (sayyid) as one whose obedience has been made divinely obligatory, equating the obligation to obey Ali with the obligation to obey the Prophet himself. This hadith was recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in his Amali, reflecting a broader tradition in Shi'a hadith literature that establishes Ali's divinely-appointed authority.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to me. He said: Bakr b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Tamim b. Bahlul narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Salih b. Abi Salama al-Nasiyyini narrated to us. He said: Abu `Awana narrated to us from Abi Bishr from Sa`id b. Jubayr from `A’isha. She said:

I was with the Messenger of Allah (s) and `Ali b. Abi Talib came forward. So, he said: This is the Master of the Arabs. So, I said: O Messenger of Allah! Are you not the Master of the Arabs? He said: I am the Master of the Children of Adam, and `Ali is the Master of the Arabs. So, I said: What is a Master? He said: One to whom obedience is made obligatory; just as obedience to me was made obligatory.
